# Configuration reference

Settings come from the environment, then from the config file (`jira config path`), then from the defaults.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `JIRA_BASE_URL` | (empty) | Base URL of Jira, including the context path if there is one. Example: `https://jira.example.com/jira`. |
| `JIRA_PAT` | secret | Personal access token. Save it with `jira setup-pat`; it is never printed. |
| `JIRA_PROJECT` | (empty) | Current project; used when --project is left out. Set it with `jira use KEY`. Example: `PROJ`. |
| `JIRA_API_PATH` | `/rest/api/2` | REST API path below the base URL. |
| `JIRA_CA_BUNDLE` | (empty) | PEM file with the certificate authorities to trust, for a private company CA. Empty: the system store. Example: `C:/certs/company-ca.pem`. |
| `JIRA_INSECURE` | `false` | Do not verify TLS certificates. Only as a temporary diagnostic. |
| `JIRA_ALLOW_HTTP` | `false` | Allow a plain http:// JIRA_BASE_URL. The token then travels unencrypted, so use it only on an isolated network. Addresses on this computer (localhost) are always allowed. |
| `JIRA_REPORTER` | (empty) | User name used as reporter when creating issues. Empty: the token's user. |
| `JIRA_HIDE_USERS` | `false` | Policy: never print people (names, e-mail addresses). `--with-users` is then refused. |
| `JIRA_EPIC_LINK_FIELD` | (empty) | Field id of Epic Link. Empty: found by its name. Example: `customfield_10002`. |
| `JIRA_STORY_POINTS_FIELD` | (empty) | Field id of Story Points. Empty: found by its name. Example: `customfield_10001`. |
| `JIRA_SPRINT_FIELD` | (empty) | Field id of Sprint. Empty: found by its name. |
| `JIRA_ACCEPTANCE_FIELD` | (empty) | Field id of the acceptance criteria. Empty: found by its name. Example: `customfield_10004`. |
| `JIRA_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` | `10` | Seconds to wait for the connection. |
| `JIRA_MAX_TIME` | `120` | Seconds to wait for an answer. |
| `JIRA_RETRY` | `2` | Retries of a read request after a network error or HTTP 429/502/503/504. Writes are never retried. |
| `JIRA_OUTPUT` | `text` | `json` makes every command that supports it print JSON, as if --json was given. Meant for scripts and agents. Example: `json`. |
| `JIRA_NO_CACHE` | `false` | Do not use the local cache of field and issue type lists. |
